headline: FRANCHISE DATAPOINT (Hormuz by the Numbers)
dek: As of 03:30 UTC Nov 5 (07:30 ), no AIS-visible commercial ship had crossed the Strait of Hormuz yet on Nov 5. On Nov 4, 5 commercial ships crossed (1 inbound, 4 outbound, including 1 tanker); most recent detected crossing CECI (bulk carrier), inbound, Nov 4 10:33 UTC.
sources: hormuz.now status page (AIS tracker, not in source-registry; attribution only)
fault_line: Open or shut? The tracker says ~10% of normal traffic; the US says its corridor keeps the strait open — which number describes reality for shippers?

sections.what_happened: As of 03:30 UTC Nov 5 (07:30 ), no AIS-visible commercial ship had crossed the Strait of Hormuz yet on Nov 5. On Nov 4, 5 commercial ships crossed (1 inbound, 4 outbound, including 1 tanker); most recent detected crossing CECI (bulk carrier), inbound, Nov 4 10:33 UTC. 7-day average 8.9 crossings/day, about 10% of normal (84.8/day pre-crisis baseline). Status: Restricted; JMIC threat level SEVERE. PORTWATCH BACKBONE GAP: newest IMF PortWatch snapshot remains portwatch-2026-10-26.json, STALE (latest observation 2026-10-18: 4 transits, 7-day avg 3.7 vs 2025 baseline 85.5/day) — no fresh IMF counted figure exists, so the hormuz.now tracker figure is cited as a tracker figure, never as an IMF counted figure.
sections.what_verified: Single tracker source; hormuz.now has no declared tier in the registry and does not count toward corroboration. Directionally consistent with the stale IMF PortWatch snapshot (single-digit daily transits vs ~85/day baseline), but the two series use different methods and dates and are not combined.
sections.what_disputed: Tracker coverage is AIS-visible commercial traffic only; non-AIS or naval movements are invisible to it. US-coordinated corridor crossings and Iranian permit claims are not reconciled in this figure.
sections.why_matters: Franchise datapoint only — feed the next Hormuz by the Numbers check, do not build a standalone Short on a 5-crossing day without a fresh counted source or a new claimant figure to test it against.
sections.context: Background: FRANCHISE DATAPOINT (Hormuz by the Numbers) — hormuz.now Nov 5 status: 0 crossings so far today; Nov 4 total 5 crossings; 7-day average 8.9/day vs 84.8 pre-crisis baseline

totw_analysis: Our read: Franchise datapoint only — feed the next Hormuz by the Numbers check, do not build a standalone Short on a 5-crossing day without a fresh counted source or a new claimant figure to test it against. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Open or shut? The tracker says ~10% of normal traffic; the US says its corridor keeps the strait open — which number describes reality for shippers?
